text:
A lightweight local proxy between your agent and its model server. It checks every tool call the model makes before the harness sees it, and swaps the calls it blocks for a text notice, so the harness runs nothing. It works with any harness that lets you set a base URL (Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, OpenCode, ...), over OpenAI Chat Completions or Anthropic Messages, streaming or not.

You want to plug a decision model in the loop? Pick one of the decision model from safeagents judge bench leaderboard.

 How it works

Each tool call goes through three stages:

1. Request-only checks. A call is blocked if it uses a tool the request never declared (tools loaded on demand through Claude Code's ToolSearch count as declared), or if its arguments contain a host (URL or bare IP) that appears nowhere in the conversation. The model's own earlier turns don't count. Calls against the proxy itself (stopping or killing it, editing /.safeagents , redirecting the harness's base URL) are blocked too.
2. atif-scan checks. The conversation becomes an ATIF trace, so atif-scan's detectors run on the pending call: reading /proc/1/environ , curl --noproxy , a Kubernetes service-account token, unshare / nsenter , ... Findings at or above --block-severity (default high ) are blocked, milder ones make the call suspicious. The examples above are all medium , so with the defaults they make a call suspicious, not blocked.
3. Decision model (optional). Suspicious calls go to a judge model, which answers allow or block .

 Without a judge, stage 2 blocks only at high and above. A suspicious call passes unchanged and the agent sees nothing. It shows up only as a WARN line in the monitor or proxy log and in the journal ( /.safeagents/calls.jsonl , see Watching the calls). For example, cat /proc/1/environ is a medium finding and runs in the default configuration. To stop such calls, configure a judge or lower --block-severity to medium .

The judge only sees what the user wrote, the tool call and the findings, never the agent's reasoning or tool results, since an agent that wants a call to run would argue its case there. It can add blocks but never lift one, and clean calls never reach it.

Streaming adds no latency: each tool call is held until its arguments are complete (harnesses only run complete calls), then released byte for byte or replaced. Text is forwarded as it arrives. atif-scan costs about 10 to 20 ms per call on an M-series Mac.

 Plugins

 --plugin MODULE:FACTORY (or path/to/file.py:FACTORY , or hf://OWNER/REPO for a plugin on the Hub, below) adds your own atif-scan checks, with the same convention as atif-scan's --plugin : FACTORY() returns a list of detectors, rules and allowances. Detectors and rules at or above --block-severity block, like the built-in ones. An allowance excuses the findings of the checks it covers, for a task that legitimately does what a check flags. --allow-host adds hosts calls may reach.

 

 

From Python, pass them to the scanner: Config(scanner=Scanner(load plugin("my pack:checks"))) .

 Plugins on the Hugging Face Hub

A plugin can live in a Hub repo as a single Python file, and be loaded by name:

 

The full form is hf://[TYPE/]OWNER/REPO[@REV][/FILE][:FACTORY] :

- TYPE : datasets/ or spaces/ for those repos; a model repo when left out.
- @REV : a branch, tag or commit.
- /FILE : the file in the repo; by default the only .py file at the repo's root.
- :FACTORY : checks by default.

The file is downloaded once and cached by huggingface hub , so it also loads offline ( HF HUB OFFLINE=1 ); a private repo needs a token ( hf auth login or HF TOKEN ). The plugin runs as code in the proxy's process, so load plugins only from repos you trust, and pin a commit ( hf://harness-hub/qwen-safeagents-plugin@ ) for reproducible runs.

 Community plugins

Plugins shared on the Hub are gathered in the safeagents plugins collection. For example, harness-hub/safeagents-dotenv-plugin blocks commands that send a .env file or a credential over the network:

 

 Publishing trajectories

 safeagents scrub finds what you shouldn't share in agent trajectories (ATIF traces, session logs, any JSON, JSON lines or text): credentials, using atif-scan's credential detection (API keys, tokens, auth headers, private keys, secret-named values, URL passwords), the values of your own secret environment variables, emails, home directories and public IP addresses. A credential found once is masked wherever else it appears, even printed bare.

 

To review what will be removed, add --show : each distinct value once, credentials first, with a count and where it was first seen ( --show-all lists every occurrence, --reveal prints values in full):

 

 safeagents publish does the same, checks the redacted copies again, and uploads only those to a Hugging Face dataset (private unless you pass --public ), with your hf auth login token:

 

JSON stays valid JSON (keys are redacted too), and files with nothing to redact are uploaded byte for byte. Redaction is best-effort: read the report before publishing. From Python: Scrubber().scrub(trace) returns the redacted trace and the findings.

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
On macOS, Linux or WSL:

curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/safeagents/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

On Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/safeagents/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex

The script installs uv if it's missing, installs safeagents as a uv tool and puts it on your PATH. Open a new terminal afterwards. To install a specific tag or commit, set SAFEAGENTS_VERSION first. Running the script again updates safeagents.

Start a proxy in the background, then point your agent at it:

$ safeagents start https://api.anthropic.com --log-only
1  http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> https://api.anthropic.com  (log: ~/.safeagents/run/1.log)

$ ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 claude

Manage the running proxies:

$ safeagents ls
1   pid 82837   http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> https://api.anthropic.com  started 2026-10-29 22:26:58  --log-only
$ safeagents stop 1
stopped 1  http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> https://api.anthropic.com

--log-only only reports what it would block, which is a good way to start. Drop it to block for real. All commands and options are in docs/commands.md, and setup guides for 14 coding agents and OpenRouter in docs/.
